question: A 34-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 3 hours after being bitten by a rattlesnake. He was hiking in the Arizona desert when he accidentally stepped on the snake and it bit his right leg. His pulse is 135/min and blood pressure is 104/81 mm Hg. Examination shows right lower leg swelling, ecchymosis, and blistering. Right ankle dorsiflexion elicits severe pain. A manometer inserted in the lateral compartment of the lower leg shows an intracompartmental pressure of 67 mm Hg. In addition to administration of the antivenom, the patient undergoes fasciotomy. Two weeks later, he reports difficulty in walking. Neurologic examination shows a loss of sensation over the lower part of the lateral side of the right leg and the dorsum of the right foot. Right foot eversion is 1/5. There is no weakness in dorsiflexion. Which of the following nerves is most likely injured in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Rattlesnake bite" -> "local tissue damage and swelling" -> "increased intracompartmental pressure" -> "fasciotomy performed" -> "neurologic examination shows loss of sensation" -> "loss of sensation over lateral side of leg and dorsum of foot" -> "weakness in foot eversion" -> "injury to superficial peroneal nerve" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Rattlesnake bite" -> "swelling and ecchymosis in right leg" -> "compartment syndrome develops" -> "fasciotomy performed" -> "neurologic examination reveals sensory loss" -> "sensation loss in lateral leg and dorsum of foot" -> "weakness in foot eversion" -> "superficial peroneal nerve likely injured" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Rattlesnake bite" -> "severe pain and swelling in right leg" -> "high intracompartmental pressure" -> "fasciotomy performed" -> "patient reports difficulty walking" -> "loss of sensation in specific areas" -> "weakness in eversion" -> "superficial peroneal nerve injury" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Rattlesnake bite" -> "right leg swelling and blistering" -> "compartment syndrome indicated by pressure of 67 mm Hg" -> "fasciotomy performed" -> "neurologic exam shows sensory deficits" -> "loss of sensation over lateral leg and dorsum of foot" -> "weakness in eversion suggests nerve injury" -> "superficial peroneal nerve most likely affected" -> 75%
analysis: The clinical presentation suggests an injury to the superficial peroneal nerve. The patient exhibits loss of sensation over the lower part of the lateral side of the leg and the dorsum of the foot, which corresponds to the sensory distribution of the superficial peroneal nerve. Additionally, the weakness in foot eversion (1/5) indicates a motor deficit in the muscles innervated by this nerve. The deep peroneal nerve primarily affects dorsiflexion and sensation between the first and second toes, which is not consistent with the symptoms described. The tibial nerve primarily affects plantar flexion and sensation in the sole of the foot, which is also not consistent. The sural nerve provides sensation to the posterior lateral aspect of the leg and does not account for the motor weakness. The saphenous nerve is a branch of the femoral nerve and does not innervate the areas affected. Therefore, the superficial peroneal nerve is the most likely injured nerve in this case.
